- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.
- If sentiment turns bearish (negative) within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust downward — apply downward bias of 1–3% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >+10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to err on the side of overconfidence — use 10–20% lower forecast than model’s baseline if sentiment is 0.00 or -0.50.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag — if true outcome shows strong upward trend, model often lags by 2–4 days — adjust forecast to align with 10–14 day moving average of true values.
